mapping.strategy:
Let S be the device-0 multiprocessor count passed by the wrapper,
Wub=(ceil_div(M,Bm)+E)*Tn and C=max(1,min(Wub,2*S)).
Submit C CTAs of 256 threads; C is not a simultaneous residency claim.

Schedule but execute no worktiles. Each actual submission has new

memo hit; tensor contents are never memoized. Recorded execution
retains its host-bound parameters and reads current device contents.

verb.initialize: Cooperatively copy m_indptr into Schedule, rendezvous, have the CTA leader form prefix, and rendezvous again. Both arrays remain live for the worker, including when it owns no tiles.
verb.prepare: Decode Work(t) from Schedule according to the assigned w. Warp h owns rows [32*floor(h/4),32*(floor(h/4)+1)) and columns [32*(h%4),32*(h%4+1)) of Dot and F. The copy and output-store work is distributed across all role members.

load.meaning: Stage(t,p) issues and commits one per-thread copy group. For p<KB, fill A(t,p), B(t,p) and AS(t,p) with A_tile(p), B_tile(p) and sa(p,u). The predicated A and scale copies zero-fill rows u>=V without reading them; B is loaded fully. Done covers every participating thread's transfers. For p>=KB, commit an empty group, with no storage write; its issue and completion events still exist.

verb.acquire: Ready(t,kb) waits until all but the newest committed group have completed on each thread, then rendezvous the CTA. Done makes the current stage readable by every warp and joins the previous Block's reads before the next refill overwrites its slot. Stage indices restart at zero per worktile.
verb.compute: Block(t,kb) performs block_dot into the register Dot, reads AS(t,kb) and the corresponding global b_scale, and performs scaled_sum into F. Dot is initialized anew for this block. All Bm rows participate, including discarded rows. Done ends the block's operand and scale reads and its Dot consumption; the next acquire joins all warps before any input-slot reuse.
verb.drain: Copies(t) waits for every committed copy group to finish, including the final empty groups, and rendezvous the CTA. InputRing is then free of input readers and in-flight writes.
verb.publish: Convert the entire final F to BF16 in Output(t), using the first InputRing slot after drain. This view holds the Bm-by-Bn block plus implementation row padding, within that slot's capacity. A CTA rendezvous makes every staged row readable. Schedule remains disjoint and live.
verb.store: Cooperatively read Output(t) and issue ordinary vector stores to the owned out region for rows u<V only. Done includes the trailing CTA rendezvous and ends all staging reads, permitting the next worktile to overwrite InputRing. Destination writes are covered by main.kernel_done; no host synchronization or separate asynchronous bulk-store queue is introduced.

initialize.meaning: Schedule is the CTA-cooperative entry: copy m_indptr and have the leader compute prefix; initialize empty resource generations and allocate ProductRing with the issuing warp. Completion includes the CTA entry rendezvous before role divergence. Schedule stores the boundaries and prefix.

verb.load: The elected lane loads Operands(n), the two A_tile/B_tile pairs for work t and pair q. A transfers cover H rows; rows beyond the global M extent are zero-filled, rows above H retain their previous storage without initialization. B transfers cover Bn rows. Completion covers all actual transfer bytes, not the untouched A rows. Ring position and completion generations continue across worktiles. Bstream is the actual submitted bstream flag: policy defaults it to zero on a failed or invalid host read, otherwise sets it when copied total row tiles equal copied nonempty groups; cache hits reuse the flag and graph execution uses its recorded value.

verb.mma: NI=2 when Wub*Q >= 48*C, otherwise NI=1; it is fixed from the submitted scalar parameters for this worker's lifetime. With one member its elected lane issues both block products; with two, one elected lane issues each block. A_pair(n) and B_pair(n) are the two operand views of Operands(n). They produce DotPair(n), containing Dot(2*q) and Dot(2*q+1), each independently initialized by its first reduction slice. The action's completion joins all NI member completions: both products are readable and all operand reads have ended. The same completion releases the operand stage to Producer.

verb.prepare: Work(t) decodes its coordinates from Schedule and initializes F to the mathematical initial state. Each epilogue member owns disjoint rows and all Bn columns of those rows. Define Full(t)=1 when V=Bm, otherwise 0. All Bm rows participate in computation and release, including discarded rows.

prefetch_a.meaning: AS(t,p) commits one row-private copy group for both scales of pair p when p<Q. Rows with r0+u>=M receive zero without reading the source; rows in another physical group are still read. For p>=Q an empty group is committed and no scale slot is written. Each worktile primes two groups, then commits one replacement per consumed pair. The final two groups are empty; the group stream is not explicitly drained or reset at worktile boundaries.

prefetch_b.meaning: BS(t,p) loads both weight scales for pair p into WeightPrefetch, replicated for epilogue rows, when p<Q; p=Q assigns zeros without global reads. Captured current scales survive overwriting these prefetch registers.

verb.capture: Scales(n) waits until all but the newest committed activation copy group are complete, then captures AS(t,q) and BS(t,q) in CurrentScales. Its done ends this pair's scale-slot reads. The next weight pair can be prefetched before DotPair is ready.
verb.acquire: DotPair(n) waits for both products to be ready and establishes their visibility to the epilogue. It then evaluates both mathematical Scale values, replacing the captured raw scales in CurrentScales and retaining the products through this pair.

read.meaning: Fragment(n,d) asynchronously reads all Bm rows of columns [32*(d%4),32*(d%4+1)) from block floor(d/4) of DotPair(n) into DrainRegister. Done guarantees that this TMEM read and register delivery have completed.

verb.await: Complete only after the explicitly referenced fragment delivery is guaranteed.
verb.compute: Accum(n,d) consumes Fragment(n,d) and the corresponding retained Scale values to perform scaled_sum for those columns. Each scale product is reused across its four column fragments. Done ends all reads of that register fragment and updates F.
verb.release: DotPair(n) joins the read completion of every epilogue row and returns its TMEM pair slot; the final register FMA has not yet executed. Staging(t,f) instead waits, through the bulk source-read completion primitive, for every outstanding earlier full-tile store to stop reading OutputStaging, then rendezvous all epilogue members. The first full tile has no earlier store to wait for. Tail tiles retain this store history.
verb.publish: Output(t,f) converts F to BF16 in OutputStaging for a full tile; all writers publish to the asynchronous access domain and rendezvous before the elected store lane may proceed.

store.meaning: Output(t,f) issues the two full-height 64-column bulk transfers to the owned out region and commits them as one group. Done means global writes are complete. The next worktile may start while these writes remain in flight.

verb.store_tail: out(t,z) converts and directly stores only rows u<V; discarded rows do not write, and OutputStaging and prior bulk-store history remain untouched. F is no longer read when this action completes.
verb.drain: Stores waits for global completion of all previously issued bulk-store groups, or has no data effect when none were issued. The final CTA rendezvous and ProductRing deallocation follow role completion, including for workers with no worktiles.

initialize.meaning: Schedule is the CTA-cooperative entry: copy m_indptr, build prefix, initialize resource generations and allocate ProductRing with the issuing warp. Completion includes the CTA rendezvous before role divergence. Schedule holds boundaries and prefix. Let J=1 for the submitted F instance and J=2 for G; these instances are defined in dispatch.when. Set R=5-J for this worker's lifetime. ProductRing holds two independent Dot blocks.

verb.load: The elected lane loads A_tile(kb) and B_tile(kb) into A_block(n) and B_block(n), jointly named Operands(n). The A box covers H rows and zero-fills beyond global M; rows above H retain their storage contents. B covers all Bn columns. Done covers all actual transfer bytes, without requiring a write to untouched A rows. Ring positions and generations continue across worktiles. Bstream is the submitted bstream flag: on a policy miss it is zero after a failed or invalid host read, otherwise one exactly when copied row tiles equal copied nonempty groups. Policy hits reuse the flag; graph replay uses the value recorded in that graph.

verb.mma: The elected lane computes Dot(kb) into Product(n) using the four reduction slices defined by block_dot, initializing on the first slice. Done is the committed completion that makes the product readable and ends all reads of Operands(n). Producer and Epilogue observe this same completion for different purposes.

verb.prepare: Work(t) decodes coordinates from Schedule and initializes F to its mathematical initial state. Two four-warp groups each own all Bm rows and one disjoint ScaleN-column group; within each group, members own disjoint rows. All Bm rows participate in computation and release. Let Full(t)=1 if V=Bm, otherwise 0.

prefetch.meaning: RawScale(t,p) loads the activation and weight scales of block p into ScalePrefetch when p<KB. Activation scales are replicated across column groups; weight scales across rows. A row beyond global M receives zero without reading a_scale, while rows in another physical group are still read. For p>=KB both scales are set to zero, complete at issue, and perform no global read. Each worktile primes blocks 0 and 1; consuming block kb allows replacement by kb+2. The captured Scale survives that replacement.

verb.capture: Scale(n) consumes RawScale(t,kb) and computes mathematical Scale(kb) into CurrentScale. Done ends those raw-scale reads. Each row and column group's scale is retained through all four fragment accumulations of this block.
verb.acquire: Product(n) observes the issuer's committed completion and establishes TMEM visibility before any fragment is read.

read.meaning: Fragment(n,d) reads columns [32*d,32*(d+1)) of each column group from Product(n) into DrainRegister for all Bm rows. Done includes delivery of both groups' fragments into registers.

verb.await: Complete after the referenced TMEM fragment delivery has finished.
verb.compute: Accum(n,d) uses Fragment(n,d) and the retained Scale(n) to perform scaled_sum for those columns in F. Done ends reads of the fragment, permitting that DrainRegister slot to be reused.
verb.release: Product(n) joins completed TMEM reads from all epilogue rows and both column groups, returning its slot before the final register FMA. Staging(t,f) instead waits for every outstanding earlier bulk store to stop reading OutputStaging, then rendezvous all epilogue members. The first batch has no prior store to wait for; later batches include stores from this or earlier worktiles. Tail worktiles preserve this bulk-store history.
verb.publish: Output(t,f) converts the J column groups numbered J*f through J*f+J-1 from F to BF16 in OutputStaging. All epilogue members rendezvous; the writers publish their data to the asynchronous access domain before the elected store lane proceeds.

store.meaning: Output(t,f) issues 2*J full-height 64-column bulk transfers to out starting at column c0+J*f*ScaleN and commits one group. Done means destination writes are complete. The next batch or worktile may advance while those writes remain in flight.

verb.store_tail: out(t,z) converts and directly stores F for rows u<V in both column groups. Other rows do not write. Done ends all F reads; OutputStaging and the prior bulk-store history are untouched.
verb.drain: Stores waits for destination completion of all earlier bulk groups; it has no data effect when none were issued. After all roles finish, the CTA rendezvous precedes ProductRing deallocation, including for workers assigned no worktiles.

initialize.meaning: Schedule is the CTA-cooperative entry: copy m_indptr, build prefix, initialize resource generations and allocate ProductRing with the issuing warp. Completion includes the CTA rendezvous before role divergence. Schedule holds boundaries and prefix. Let J=1 when this phase uses L[q]=F and J=2 when L[q]=G, with q bound by work_schedule. Set R=5-J for this worker's lifetime. ProductRing holds two independent Dot blocks. Each launch starts its own ring positions, generations, scale state and store history; no local resource or event instance is shared between first and retry.

initialize.meaning: Schedule is the CTA-cooperative entry: copy m_indptr, build prefix, initialize resource generations and allocate ProductRing with the issuing warp. Completion includes the CTA rendezvous before role divergence. Schedule holds boundaries and prefix. Let J=1 when this phase uses L[q]=F and J=2 when L[q]=G, with q bound by work_schedule. Set R=5-J for this worker's lifetime. ProductRing holds two independent Dot blocks. Each launch starts its own ring positions, generations, scale state and store history; no local resource or event instance is shared among first, retry and final.

verb.load: The elected lane loads A_tile(kb) and B_tile(kb) into A_block(n) and B_block(n), jointly named Operands(n). The A box covers H rows and zero-fills beyond global M; rows above H retain their storage contents. B covers all Bn columns. Done covers all actual transfer bytes, without requiring a write to untouched A rows. Ring positions and generations continue across worktiles. Bstream is the submitted bstream flag: on a policy miss it is zero after a failed or invalid host read, otherwise one exactly when copied row tiles equal copied nonempty groups. Policy hits reuse the flag; graph replay uses the value recorded in that graph.
